unit.why: A short memorate: the narrator tells how the Neskhiz rebbe, late in life, had him buy the Noda bi-Yehuda, ordered the volumes bound and shelved, and explained the gesture with a saying of the Besht.
unit.boundary_note: Ends with the section heading 'מענין נסיון', which introduces the next division.

stories.start_quote: ואעירה לי אשר מרן מנעסכיז זצל"ה
stories.summary_en: Near the end of his life the Neskhiz rebbe asks his disciple what is new in the beit midrash, sends him to buy the Noda bi-Yehuda from a newly arrived bookseller, and has it bound and shelved; when the disciple is puzzled, the rebbe explains that the Besht said the Noda bi-Yehuda's author had a new soul, hidden on high until he came into the world.

quotes: וציווני ליתן לקשור אותם ולהעמידם בין הספרים
tags.why: The rebbe instructs his attendant-disciple, who is the narrator.
The puzzled disciple learns the hidden reason for the rebbe's reverence for the book.

quotes: היה לו נשמה חדשה שלא היתה עדיין בעולם
tags.why: The Besht supernaturally knows the origin of a soul.
The beit midrash is the frame where the bookseller arrives.

quotes: הג׳ הצדיק בעל נוב״י היה לו נשמה חדשה
tags.why: Praises the holiness of a non-Hasidic rabbinic authority, though within a Hasidic frame.

quotes: והיתה גנוזה במרומים עד שבא הוא לעולם
tags.why: The upper worlds are mentioned as the place where the soul was stored; not really a setting.

missing_concepts: new soul (נשמה חדשה) vs. reincarnated soul
Hasidic esteem for a non-Hasidic halakhist (Noda bi-Yehuda)
